title: Deviation investigation assistant
client: A fictional oral solid dose manufacturer with one site, a validated eQMS and an MES.
pain: Deviations close late, root causes often say 'human error', and repeat deviations are rising. Investigators spend much of their time searching for similar past events and chasing lab data.
data: Synthetic export of 300 closed deviations (id, dates, area, product, batch, description, root cause category, CAPA link) with deliberate messy categories, plus 20 synthetic LIMS results linked to some batches.
deliver: A profile of the deviation data with a list of quality issues and a cleaned category list.
A search that returns the five most similar past deviations for a new one.
An assistant that drafts a summary and candidate root causes into a separate, attributed field, never into the approved record.
An evaluation set of 30 cases with expected root causes and a scored run against agreed acceptance criteria.
approval: The investigator writes and submits the final investigation; QA approves it in the eQMS with an electronic signature.
measure: Share of drafts whose candidate root cause matches the investigator's final cause, and investigator time per deviation compared with a baseline sample.

title: Batch record review by exception
client: A fictional sterile injectables CDMO using electronic batch records for most steps and paper for a few.
pain: QA reviews every page of every batch record, and review is the longest wait between end of manufacture and release.
data: Synthetic batch records for 40 batches as JSON (steps, set points, recorded values, operator IDs, timestamps, free-text comments), with planted exceptions such as out-of-range values, missing second-person checks and late entries.
deliver: Rules that flag structured exceptions such as values outside limits, missing checks and entries made long after the step.
An LLM step that reads free-text comments and flags those that may need QA attention, with a short reason.
A review screen mock-up that shows flags first and links each flag to the source entry.
A test report showing every planted exception was flagged, and the false flag rate.
approval: The QA reviewer reviews flags and the full record as the SOP requires, and signs the batch record review in the MES.
measure: Share of planted exceptions caught (target: all of them), false flags per batch, and reviewer minutes per batch in a timed trial.

title: IQ/OQ protocol drafting from a URS
client: A fictional API manufacturer installing a new dryer and updating its validation templates.
pain: Validation engineers write IQ and OQ protocols by hand from the URS and vendor documents, and traceability between requirements and tests is kept in a spreadsheet that drifts.
data: A synthetic URS with 40 requirements, a synthetic vendor functional specification, and two approved protocol templates.
deliver: A traceability matrix generated from the URS, linking each requirement to a proposed test.
Draft IQ and OQ test steps in the client's template, each citing the requirement it covers.
A gap report listing requirements with no test and tests with no requirement.
A review checklist the validation lead uses to approve or reject each drafted test.
approval: The validation engineer edits and owns the protocol; QA approves it before execution.
measure: Share of requirements covered by an accepted test, number of drafted steps the validation lead rejects, and drafting time compared with the last manual protocol.

title: Change control impact assessment helper
client: A fictional multi-product tablet site with about 1,500 controlled documents.
pain: Every change request needs an impact assessment listing affected SOPs, batch records, validation documents and training. Reviewers often miss affected documents, and changes come back for rework.
data: Synthetic document index (id, title, type, owner, linked equipment and products) for 300 documents, and 25 synthetic past change requests with the documents they actually affected.
deliver: A search that proposes affected documents for a new change request, with the reason for each.
A draft impact assessment in the client's change control form layout.
An evaluation against the 25 past changes showing which affected documents were found and which were missed.
A one-page design note covering intended use, approval point, audit trail and change control for the tool itself.
approval: The change owner confirms the list and writes the assessment; QA approves the change request in the eQMS.
measure: Recall of truly affected documents on past changes (missed documents matter most), and rework rate of change requests in a pilot.

title: CDMO batch documentation review for IMP release
client: A fictional small sponsor running two clinical trials with drug product made at an outside CDMO.
pain: The sponsor's quality team checks each batch package (batch record summary, certificate of analysis, deviations, shipping temperature data) against specifications and the quality agreement by hand, and release dates slip.
data: Ten synthetic batch packages with certificates of analysis as text, a synthetic specification table, deviation summaries and shipping temperature logs, with planted issues such as a result at the limit, an unclosed deviation and a temperature excursion.
deliver: Extraction of CoA results into a table and comparison against the specification.
A checklist review that flags open deviations, missing documents and temperature excursions.
A one-page review summary per batch, with every flag linked to its source page.
A test report showing each planted issue was found.
approval: The sponsor's qualified quality reviewer makes the release decision and signs it; the tool only prepares the review.
measure: Planted issues found (target: all), extraction accuracy of CoA values, and review time per batch package.

title: CPV trending and signal summary
client: A fictional generic drug manufacturer with one high-volume product in continued process verification.
pain: Engineers pull assay, dissolution and process data from LIMS and the historian into spreadsheets each quarter, so trends are spotted late and the CPV report takes weeks.
data: Synthetic results for 120 batches (assay, dissolution, hardness, key process parameters) with a planted upward drift in one parameter and two batches out of trend.
deliver: A script that builds control charts with limits from the first 30 batches and flags rule breaks.
A plain-language draft of the signal summary for the CPV report, citing the batches and charts behind each statement.
A data check report confirming every value traces back to a source record.
A short note on what would need validating before the scripts are used for the real CPV report.
approval: The process engineer reviews the charts and draft, and the CPV report is approved under the site's procedure.
measure: Planted drift and out-of-trend batches detected, statements in the draft that trace to data (target: all), and time to produce the quarterly report.
